items.title: [macOS] Codex Desktop: Computer-use subprocess accumulation, excessive memory footprint and severe UI slowdown

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
[macOS] Codex Desktop: Computer-use subprocess accumulation, excessive memory footprint and severe UI slowdown

Product: ChatGPT / Codex Desktop for macOS
Date reproduced: October 21, 2026
Platform: Apple Silicon MacBook Pro, 16 GB unified memory
Desktop version: 26.1013.40934 (reported client version; confirm in About Codex)
Subscription: ChatGPT Pro
Severity: High — materially impairs normal development work

Summary

Codex Desktop exhibits substantial resource consumption and progressive responsiveness degradation during normal development workflows.

The application has reported a memory footprint as high as 31.47 GB on a 16 GB MacBook Pro, accompanied by 16.59 GB of swap usage.

A controlled single-thread test revealed accumulation of computer-use-related subprocesses (cua_node, node_repl, and Codex Computer Use) from 22 immediately after restart to 61 after the task had finished.

The problem is not limited to high concurrency. Significant resource consumption occurs with a single active development thread.

Development environment

  • Multiple local Git repositories

  • Hundreds of historical Codex conversations displayed in the sidebar

  • SSH-based development and remote administration

  • Occasional RDP and graphical computer-use workflows

  • Multiple concurrent Codex sessions during normal use

  • Previous conversations and repositories restored when the application starts

Observed behavior

1. Excessive application memory footprint

Observation | Reported measurement -- | -- Peak ChatGPT/Codex application footprint | 31.47 GB Swap file at peak | 16.59 GB Available RAM at peak | 3.24 GB Memory pressure indicator | 64% Single-thread test, after ~5 minutes | 11.57 GB

Processes were counted using:

ps -axo command | grep -E 'cua_node|Codex Computer Use' | grep -v grep | wc -l

Most inspected subprocesses consumed approximately 5–17 MB of resident memory, reported negligible CPU utilization, and remained alive for more than 20 minutes.

Many were descendants of the Codex app-server process.

The process-count increase is reproducible. Whether the workers are intentionally retained or leaking has not been established.

3. Renderer memory behavior

Following an application restart, eight renderer processes collectively consumed approximately 2.12 GB RSS after 2.5 minutes.

During a subsequent single-thread test, combined renderer RSS decreased to 1.28 GB after approximately 25 minutes.

This indicates renderer resident memory can decrease during active operation. A continuously growing renderer leak has not been demonstrated.

4. System performance degradation

The user experienced severe UI responsiveness problems, including unusually slow screenshot loading.

macOS diagnostics showed:

  • Approximately 6.62 GB compressed memory

  • Approximately 15 GB physical memory in use

  • 130 MB unused physical memory

  • CPU approximately 80% idle

  • Significant cumulative compression and swap activity

The slowdown appears more consistent with memory-management or application responsiveness issues than sustained CPU saturation, although the immediate cause has not been isolated.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Launch Codex Desktop with existing repository and conversation history.

  2. Allow the application to restore its previous workspace.

  3. Record computer-use subprocess count and renderer RSS.

  4. Run one normal development thread using SSH and repository operations.

  5. Repeat measurements periodically.

  6. Allow the task to complete.

  7. Leave Codex open and idle.

  8. Measure subprocess count again.

Observed: Computer-use-related process count increases during execution and can continue increasing after task completion.

Expected behavior

Codex should support concurrent development sessions across multiple repositories without progressive degradation of the desktop application.

Computer-use workers should have a bounded lifecycle or demonstrably bounded resource footprint. Completed tasks should not indefinitely accumulate unnecessary resources.

Historical conversation lists should not cause disproportionate memory usage.

Engineering investigation requested

Please investigate:

  1. Lifecycle management and cleanup of cua_node, node_repl, and Codex Computer Use subprocesses.

  2. Whether computer-use environments are being created unnecessarily for primarily SSH-based workflows.

  3. Whether subprocess counts grow without a practical upper bound across completed tasks.

  4. Renderer and application memory accounting, including compressed, shared, and resident memory.

  5. The relationship between application memory footprint, macOS compression/swap activity, and UI responsiveness.

  6. Whether session restoration or historical conversation metadata contributes to initial memory allocations.

User impact

This affects a production development workflow involving multiple repositories and simultaneous Codex agents.

Repeated application restarts and limiting development to one concurrent thread are not acceptable permanent mitigations because they materially reduce productivity.

The requested outcome is reliable resource management while preserving multi-threaded, multi-repository, SSH, and computer-use functionality.

Diagnostic evidence available

  • Activity Monitor process screenshots

  • CleanMyMac memory screenshots

  • ps process hierarchy and resident-memory measurements

  • Computer-use subprocess counts across restart, execution, and idle states

  • memory_pressure output

  • top system diagnostics

Raw application logs, session transcripts, credentials, repository contents, and potentially sensitive paths should be reviewed before being shared publicly.

Status: Reproduced resource accumulation; underlying cause not yet established.

items.title: [ChatGPT Web][Remote MCP OAuth] Refresh token is not used after access token expiration; reconnect retains outdated OAuth scopes

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: auth
labels.description: Issues related to authentication and accounts

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

items.body:
## Environment

- Product: ChatGPT Web, organizational workspace
- Browser: Chromium-based, Windows
- Connector: Custom remote MCP server (Streamable HTTP)
- Authentication: OAuth Authorization Code + PKCE
- OAuth provider: Supabase Auth
- Access token lifetime: 3600 seconds
- Supported grants: `authorization_code`, `refresh_token`
- Supported scopes include `email` and `offline_access`

## Summary

Our existing custom MCP connector works immediately after OAuth authentication but loses connectivity after approximately 60 minutes.

The authorization server successfully issues a refresh token. However, no refresh-token request is observed from the ChatGPT client.

The connector was originally registered before `offline_access` was added to the server's discovery metadata.

Despite reconnecting, ChatGPT continues requesting the original OAuth scope (`email`) rather than the updated scopes.

We also observe stale MCP tool definitions, requiring a separate manual refresh in organizational workspace settings.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Authenticate an existing custom MCP connector in ChatGPT.
2. Verify that authenticated MCP tool calls work.
3. Wait 75 minutes without manually reconnecting.
4. Invoke an authenticated MCP tool.
5. Observe the authentication failure.
6. Reauthorize the existing connector.
7. Observe that ChatGPT continues requesting its originally configured OAuth scopes.

## Expected Behavior

ChatGPT should securely renew access tokens using the supported refresh-token flow, or provide a supported method to update an existing connector's OAuth configuration.

OAuth credentials should remain valid across normal sessions without repeated manual authorization.

## Actual Behavior

- Initial authorization succeeds.
- Authenticated MCP calls work before access-token expiration.
- The OAuth server issues a refresh token.
- No `grant_type=refresh_token` request is observed from ChatGPT.
- After expiration, the MCP server returns HTTP 401 with `auth.no_bearer_token`.
- ChatGPT reports `The tool failed internally`.
- Manual reconnection temporarily restores functionality.
- Updated OAuth scopes are not requested during reconnection.

## Additional Workspace Behavior

Our current recovery procedure requires opening a fresh browser session, reauthorizing the connector through personal ChatGPT settings, switching back to the organizational workspace, and manually refreshing the MCP tool definitions.

The OAuth authentication and tool-schema synchronization problems may have separate causes.

## Root Cause Hypothesis

The ChatGPT client may retain the OAuth scope configuration established during the connector's initial registration.

Although the authorization server now advertises `offline_access` and supports refresh-token grants, the existing connector continues using its original scope configuration.

This is a hypothesis based on server-side observations, not a confirmed internal ChatGPT root cause.

## Business Impact

The connector is used in an organizational environment. Requiring repeated manual authentication prevents reliable use by employees and automated workflows.

## Questions for OpenAI Engineering

1. Does ChatGPT require an explicitly granted `offline_access` scope before storing and using refresh tokens?
2. Does ChatGPT cache OAuth scopes during initial connector registration?
3. Can the OAuth configuration of an existing connector be refreshed without replacing it?
4. Why are no refresh-token requests observed after access-token expiration?
5. Can MCP tool schemas be refreshed automatically in existing organizational workspace sessions?

## Requested Resolution

Please investigate OAuth refresh-token handling and cached scope configuration for existing ChatGPT custom MCP connectors.

We would prefer a solution that preserves the existing connector and organizational configuration.

Detailed logs, endpoint addresses, OAuth client identifiers, and sanitized authorization records can be provided privately to OpenAI Support.

items.title: macOS desktop host overwrites externally modified source with stale contents; Endpoint Security identifies ChatGPT main process

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## What version of the Codex App are you using?

- ChatGPT desktop host / Codex surface: **26.1016.51333**, build **21161**.
- Bundle identifier: `com.openai.codex`.
- Host executable on disk: `/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/MacOS/ChatGPT`.
- Bundled Codex Framework: **155.0.8059.80** (framework bundle version **8059.80**).
- Versions were read directly from the installed bundle Info.plist files.

## What platform is your computer?

macOS **26.5.2**, build **25F84**, **arm64**.

## What issue are you seeing?

Local Kotlin source edits repeatedly disappear because a source file is rewritten with older contents while using the Codex surface in the desktop host.

We instrumented the affected file using macOS Endpoint Security (`eslogger write close rename create unlink truncate exchangedata copyfile`). A controlled external edit was subsequently overwritten by the **ChatGPT host main process itself**, not merely by a child process attributed to the host.

This report concerns local source integrity. It is not a model generating an unwanted replacement in a shell command: the captured writer executable was the desktop host main executable.

## Observed reproduction in the affected workspace

This was captured in the existing long-running development session. **A deterministic reproduction in a fresh, minimal workspace has not yet been established.**

1. Work on a local Android/Kotlin project through the Codex desktop surface. Repeated reversions of functional edits had already been observed.
2. Enable an Endpoint Security capture with root and Full Disk Access, retaining only events for the affected source file. Record file SHA-256 hashes and process identities.
3. At **2026-10-21 20:28:43 UTC+08:00**, use a known Python process, PID **48445**, to append one uniquely identifiable, behavior-neutral comment to the file. Do not rebuild the app.
4. Confirm that Endpoint Security captures this controlled process's `write` and modified `close`, and that the expected new file hash is present.
5. At **20:30:56**, verify that the external edit is still present.
6. At **20:31:11**, Endpoint Security captures the **ChatGPT main process, PID 28813**, writing the source file and closing it with `modified=true`.
7. The comment is gone and the file hash is exactly the same as the previously observed older version. The reporting agent issued no source restore/checkout command between the controlled edit and this overwrite.

The exact UI action or internal desktop subsystem triggering step 6 was not captured. Several reader-related chats shared the same workspace directory, but this is context only, not proof of a cross-chat cause.

## Endpoint Security evidence

Timestamps below are UTC+08:00; the corresponding UTC times are 12:28:43 and 12:31:11.

| Local time | Actor | Event |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 20:28:43.470 | Known Python PID 48445 | Controlled `write` |
| 20:28:43.476 | Known Python PID 48445 | `close`, modified |
| **20:31:11.483** | **ChatGPT PID 28813** | **`write` to the same source file** |
| **20:31:11.499** | **ChatGPT PID 28813** | **`close`, `modified=true`** |

The captured writer's process identity:

```json
{
  "audit_token": { "pid": 28813 },
  "ppid": 1,
  "executable": {
    "path": "/Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/MacOS/ChatGPT"
  },
  "responsible_audit_token": { "pid": 28813 }
}
```

The controlled Python writer was a distinct executable and PID. Thus this is evidence of a **direct host-process write**, not just the host being the responsible application for a Python/shell child.

File state across the host-process write:

| State | SHA-256 | Size |
| --- | --- | --- |
| External edit present | `07a12d19d95781a3f6e5077505fdbd7d679be047e792fdbe7ae29d1db5b25ffc` | 91,366 bytes |
| After host write | `648af19d2b7c15a78f0797a0ac2f602ed3e30f30ec0d9c5c4ec4b1b91bbd8be2` | 91,301 bytes |

The inode remained **149635061**; modification and change times advanced to **20:31:11.476236**. The resulting bytes matched the older version seen in previous reversions.

A subsequent planned reproduction write was **aborted by a pre-write hash assertion** because the file had already changed. It did not write or restore anything, so it cannot explain the captured host write.

## Expected behavior

The desktop host should preserve newer changes made by agent tools or external editors. Any editor/document/snapshot reconciliation should detect that on-disk content changed and reload, merge, or present a conflict rather than silently write stale contents over it.

## Impact

- Functional source changes had repeatedly reverted during this development workflow, causing rework.
- A completed build and installed binary could contain the correct fix while the source on disk had already reverted, creating misleading source/binary divergence.
- A local Git commit preserved the correct implementation, but did not prevent subsequent working-tree overwrites.

The direct, kernel-audited reproduction here proves clobbering of the controlled external comment. Earlier functional reversions were observed outside the successful audit window; this report does not claim their individual writers were all independently captured.

## Investigation boundaries and requested triage

The direct writer is established. The internal trigger is **not** established: we cannot yet distinguish editor autosave, undo/revert, document synchronization, snapshot restoration, or another host subsystem. Please investigate the host's file-writing and stale-document reconciliation paths rather than treating these hypotheses as diagnoses.

Please provide an engineering triage path and a safe mitigation for local source clobbering. If this belongs to another desktop team, please route it there.

## Privacy / diagnostics

This report intentionally omits business source code, account identifiers, workspace/username paths, full chat transcripts, and unfiltered application/system logs. The event summary above is redacted from the locally retained Endpoint Security evidence. No private source files or raw log attachments are being published.

## Follow-up: source-tab reproduction and closed-tab control (2026-10-21)

A second kernel-audited overwrite was captured in the same running session. This narrows the investigation toward the built-in source preview/editor lifecycle, but **does not identify the exact internal caller or establish a fresh-workspace deterministic reproduction**.

All times below are UTC+08:00.

1. At **20:46:04**, restore the correct committed file using a known Python process (PID **81727**). SHA-256: `ef957bfdea878dbbf4356fb0d1ee91efba6eae0baef5305a9757dd6abad26d80` (95,555 bytes).
2. Open that file in Codex's source preview/editor. The user confirms the preview is visible and reports no external-change/unsaved warning.
3. At **20:47:31**, append a behavior-neutral comment externally using known Python PID **83516**. SHA-256 becomes `fefad0987502e41d660de3a8c9a2f28b3b8be9c544bb81f2cb3e750e2865d6b6` (95,630 bytes).
4. At **20:48:39.158**, Endpoint Security records the same desktop main executable, PID **28813**, writing the file, followed by `close(modified=true)`. The resulting file is byte-for-byte the version from step 1: the external comment is lost. Receipt timestamps are 20:48:39.189 and 20:48:39.204.
5. Asked about that moment, the user reports the cursor was in the newly opened tab; no explicit accept/reject action was reported. Application logs show chat navigation in the same time window, which is correlation only, not proof of a trigger.

Unlike earlier functional reversions, this controlled reproduction discarded only the added comment: the restored functional fix remained intact. It still directly demonstrates clobbering of a newer external change by the main app process.

### Closed-tab control / provisional mitigation

The user then closed the source tab. At **20:51:20.920**, another external comment was appended (known Python PID **89464**). Through **20:53:18.429** (approximately **118 seconds**), the comment remained intact and the audit recorded **zero main-app writes to the target**. The test comment was then removed only after checking its exact expected hash; the file again matched the committed version.

Closing the affected source tab is therefore a **short-window mitigation observed in this session**, not a verified permanent fix. By comparison, the open-tab probe was overwritten about 68 seconds after the external edit. This is a single paired observation, not a controlled statistical comparison.

### Read-only inspection of the installed bundle

The shipped editor code contains both a **3,000 ms autosave timer** and a **save-on-dispose** path. The local `workspaceFiles.saveText` implementation compares the supplied expected modification time with the disk modification time, and its stat helper explicitly bypasses the stat cache. These are candidate paths for engineering inspection, **not a diagnosis**: we did not capture a JavaScript stack or runtime save arguments, and have not established why the external-change protection did not prevent this write. Please do not treat stale stat caching, autosave, or navigation as proven root causes.

Please investigate how source-tab content, external-change reconciliation, and save/disposal state interact, including why a newer disk version can be replaced without an explicit conflict-resolution action. A safe fix should preserve external changes or surface a conflict before writing older editor contents.

No business source, private paths, chat transcripts, or raw logs are included in this update.

items.body:
### Issue
Several existing chats in the Windows desktop app fail to complete ordinary responses with:

```text
stream disconnected before completion: stream closed before response.completed
```

The actual `/compact` command in each affected chat also fails with:

```text
Error running remote compact task: stream disconnected before completion: stream closed before response.completed
```

### Reproduction pattern
1. In each affected existing chat, a prompt was sent while `gpt-5.5` was selected. The app returned: `400 invalid_request_error: The 'gpt-5.5' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account.`
2. Switch the affected chat to GPT-6.1 Sol and send an ordinary short prompt. It fails with the stream-disconnection error.
3. Run the actual `/compact` command. It fails with the remote compact task error.
4. Restart the computer and retry. The affected chat still fails.

Controls: A new chat can answer a short prompt. Another existing chat that was switched away from 5.5 **before** sending a new prompt compacted successfully. This suggests that an old chat merely having 5.5 selected is insufficient to trigger the issue. The unsupported-model request is a possible trigger, not a confirmed cause.

### Expected behaviour
After switching to a supported model, ordinary prompts and `/compact` should complete. An unsupported-model request should not leave a chat unable to respond.

### Related report
This differs from #52016: there, compaction fails while ordinary conversations work. Here, ordinary responses in affected chats fail too, while other chats work.

I can provide app version and diagnostic thread IDs through a private feedback channel if needed.

### Workaround used
For work that must continue now, copy the affected chat as Markdown and paste it into a new chat set to GPT-6.1 Sol. The new chat can use the readable transcript as context without inheriting the old chat's internal session/compaction state. For a long transcript, paste it in labelled parts and ask the new chat to wait until the final part before responding.

This is a continuity workaround, **not a repair of the original chat**. I have other work I can continue and can wait for an OpenAI fix for the original histories.

Optional way to keep track: prefix the title of each affected chat (for example, `5.5 `), then archive it **after** transferring the work to a new chat. The old chat remains available as a reference. This is a personal organisation choice, not a required recovery step.

```text

```

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

### What platform is your computer?

Microsoft Windows NT 10.0.26200.0 x64

### What issue are you seeing?

After migrating Codex conversation files between two Linux accounts on the same SSH server, historical threads can be resumed through the remote CLI and are returned by the app-server's `thread/list` API, but they do not appear in the Windows Desktop sidebar.

New conversations created directly through Desktop appear and persist normally.

The issue also affects a newly forked remote thread with a unique UUID, which is not discovered by the Windows local thread catalog.

The catalog synchronization watermark remains unchanged even after triggering a new-window synchronization. This appears to involve remote SSH thread discovery and catalog reconciliation, rather than missing or corrupted session files.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Connect Windows Codex Desktop to a Linux server using Remote SSH and create some conversations.
2. Create a second SSH connection to a different Unix account on the same server, using a separate `CODEX_HOME`.
3. Copy the historical `sessions/` JSONL files to the new account, preserving existing sessions and authentication.
4. Resume an imported thread using `codex resume <UUID>` on the new account. The historical conversation loads successfully.
5. Query the new account's app-server using `thread/list` with the new workspace `cwd` and `useStateDbOnly:true`. The imported thread is returned.
6. Open the new SSH workspace in Windows Desktop. The imported thread does not appear in the sidebar.
7. Fork the imported thread using app-server `thread/fork`. A new UUID is generated, but the fork is also missing from the Desktop catalog.
8. Open another Desktop window using File → New Window to trigger catalog synchronization. The missing conversations remain invisible.

New conversations created directly in the new SSH workspace are displayed normally and survive Desktop restarts.

This is a reproduction using migrated session files, not a confirmed issue with ordinary non-migrated sessions.

### What is the expected behavior?

Windows Desktop should display remote conversations that are successfully indexed and returned by the selected SSH host's app-server.

At minimum, a thread that can be resumed by the CLI and returned by `thread/list` should be discoverable from the corresponding Desktop workspace.

The client should also provide a reliable way to refresh the remote thread catalog when synchronization becomes stale, without deleting existing conversations or resetting application state.

### Additional information

**Environment**
- Windows Codex Desktop: `26.1013.4894.0`
- Remote Codex CLI/app-server: `0.160.0`
- Two Remote SSH connections to separate Unix accounts on the same Linux HPC server

**Confirmed remote behavior**
- Historical JSONL files are present.
- `codex resume <UUID>` loads the original conversation.
- Remote SQLite integrity check: `ok`.
- App-server response: `INIT_OK`, `LISTED_THREADS: 1`, `TARGET_FOUND: True`.

**Windows local catalog**
- The imported thread has records under both SSH host IDs, with `missing_candidate=0`.
- Removing the old-host association in a backed-up test did not restore visibility; it was subsequently rediscovered.
- The imported thread and a visible new thread have matching relevant metadata, including `source=vscode`, `model_provider=openai`, `thread_source=user`, and `has_user_event=0`.
- Forking the imported thread with a new UUID did not make the fork appear in the local catalog.

**Catalog synchronization experiment**

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Watermark | 1792575587 | 1792575587 |
| Observation sequence | 53 | 54 |
| New-host catalog rows | 9 | 9 |
| Fork discovered | No | No |

Opening a new window increased the observation sequence without advancing the watermark or discovering the fork.

**Separate migration limitation**

The remote directory contains approximately 246 active session files, while its SQLite thread index contains 13 rows. We intentionally did not run bulk ScanAndRepair. However, the missing dMRI thread described above is already indexed and returned by app-server, so incomplete bulk indexing cannot fully explain the observed problem.

**Request**

Is there a supported mechanism to recover stalled Windows Remote SSH catalog synchronization and reconcile imported or forked threads without deleting client state?

Related: #27284.

Sanitized diagnostics are available upon request. No private transcripts, credentials, raw research data, or SQLite databases are attached.

### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)? openai.chatgpt@26.51007.21434 openai.codex-audio@26.1007.21434 codex-cli 0.162.1 ### What subscription do you have? ChatGPT Pro ### What platform is your computer? Linux 6.8.0-138-generic x86_64 x86_64 ### What issue are you seeing? Primary error: Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model. Codex session logs contain the following historical error occurrences: 563 "codex_error_info":"server_overloaded" 51 "codex_error_info":"usage_limit_exceeded" 1 "codex_error_info":"unauthorized" These counts represent occurrences across historical session files, not necessarily unique failed requests. [BUG] Persistent "Selected model is at capacity" across Codex models on ChatGPT Pro — Web works, VS Code unusable

Summary

I am a ChatGPT Pro subscriber experiencing persistent server_overloaded errors when using Codex on Linux, particularly through the VS Code extension.

Codex Web works with the same account, but the VS Code extension is effectively unusable. Codex CLI also experiences repeated and intermittent failures across multiple models.

This is not an isolated failure of a single model or a single request. I have reproduced the problem with different models, reasoning levels, service tiers, and configurations.

The problem has persisted despite extensive troubleshooting and is seriously disrupting my daily development and research workflow.

Environment

  • Subscription: ChatGPT Pro

  • OS: Linux (ThinkStation P3 Tower)

  • Clients: VS Code Codex extension and Codex CLI

  • Affected models: gpt-6.1-sol, gpt-5.6-sol

  • Codex Web: Working

  • VS Code Codex: Repeatedly failing

  • Codex CLI: Intermittently succeeding, frequently failing

  • Issue reproduced: October 21, 2026

Error Messages

Primary error:

Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.

Codex session logs contain the following historical error occurrences:

563 "codex_error_info":"server_overloaded"
 51 "codex_error_info":"usage_limit_exceeded"
  1 "codex_error_info":"unauthorized"

These counts represent occurrences across historical session files, not necessarily unique failed requests.

I have also observed the following error:

2026-10-21T10:50:21.449958Z ERROR codex_models_manager::manager:
failed to refresh available models: request timed out

Interestingly, a CLI request sometimes succeeds even after the model-list refresh times out.

Steps to Reproduce

Test 1: Ignore user configuration

codex exec \
  --ignore-user-config \
  --ephemeral \
  --skip-git-repo-check \
  -C /tmp \
  -s read-only \
  --json \
  "Reply exactly OK. Do not use tools."

This request succeeded once:

{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_0","type":"agent_message","text":"OK"}}
{"type":"turn.completed","usage":{"input_tokens":19610,"cached_input_tokens":12288,"cache_write_input_tokens":0,"output_tokens":5,"reasoning_output_tokens":0}}

Test 2: Same request with normal configuration

Running the same command without --ignore-user-config failed:

{"type":"error","message":"Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model."}
{"type":"turn.failed","error":{"message":"Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model."}}

Test 3: Remove the configuration file

I backed up and temporarily removed ~/.codex/config.toml, then repeated the minimal CLI request.

Result: The same capacity error persisted.

This indicates that the issue cannot be reliably resolved simply by removing the user configuration.

Test 4: Different models and service tiers

I explicitly tested multiple combinations using --ignore-user-config:

Model | Reasoning | Service Tier | Observed Result -- | -- | -- | -- gpt-6.1-sol | High | Priority | Failed: model at capacity gpt-6.1-sol | Medium | Default | Failed: model at capacity gpt-5.6-sol | Medium | Default | Succeeded in one test, but the model is not consistently reliable gpt-5.6-sol | Medium | Priority | Succeeded in one test, with model-list refresh timeout

Example failing command:

codex exec \
  --ignore-user-config \
  --ephemeral \
  --skip-git-repo-check \
  -C /tmp \
  -s read-only \
  -m gpt-6.1-sol \
  -c model_reasoning_effort=medium \
  -c 'service_tier="default"' \
  --json \
  "Reply exactly OK. Do not use tools."

Output:

{"type":"thread.started","thread_id":"01a15e14-c4f2-7180-8a09-b7f14b663c49"}
{"type":"turn.started"}
{"type":"error","message":"Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model."}
{"type":"turn.failed","error":{"message":"Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model."}}

A successful request using a different model or service tier does not represent a reliable workaround. The problem remains intermittent, and VS Code Codex is still unusable.

Troubleshooting Already Performed

  • Tested Codex Web using the same Pro account — works.

  • Tested CLI with and without --ignore-user-config.

  • Removed and backed up config.toml.

  • Tested different models.

  • Tested different reasoning levels and service tiers.

  • Used fresh ephemeral CLI sessions.

  • Reproduced errors with a trivial prompt requiring no tools, repository access, or code execution.

  • Inspected Codex session logs and confirmed a large number of server_overloaded errors.

None of these steps has provided a reliable fix.

Expected Behavior

Codex should be consistently available to an eligible ChatGPT Pro subscriber within the applicable usage limits.

If a particular model is temporarily overloaded, the client should provide accurate error information and recover when capacity becomes available.

The VS Code extension should not remain effectively unusable while Codex Web works for the same account.

Actual Behavior

  • The VS Code extension repeatedly fails with "Selected model is at capacity."

  • Multiple models are affected.

  • Simple CLI requests sometimes succeed and sometimes fail.

  • Removing user configuration does not reliably resolve the issue.

  • The client has also experienced model-list refresh timeouts.

  • Switching models is not a dependable workaround.

Representative Thread IDs

Failed requests:

01a15e12-3e99-7d93-8fdc-4f5e0c3976a6
01a15e14-c4f2-7180-8a09-b7f14b663c49

Successful requests for comparison:

01a15e12-7513-7e90-986a-521b8114a438
01a15e15-4bfe-78e0-b6bb-2952d5eab348

These successful and failed requests occurred on the same machine and ChatGPT Pro account.

Request for Investigation

Could the Codex team investigate whether this issue is related to:

  1. Server-side model capacity admission or request routing.

  2. Differences between Codex Web and local Codex CLI/IDE request paths.

  3. Account-specific serving-pool assignment or intermittent admission failures.

  4. Model-catalog refresh timeouts and possible interactions with inference requests.

  5. Misleading or overly generic server_overloaded error reporting.

I am not claiming that any particular mechanism is the root cause. The client-side evidence is insufficient to distinguish these possibilities.

However, the successful requests demonstrate that authentication and basic connectivity can work, while the repeated failures suggest a problem beyond a simple local configuration mistake.

Please investigate the supplied successful and failed thread IDs using server-side logs.

I rely heavily on Codex for daily software development and robotics research. The persistent failures significantly reduce the usability of my paid Pro subscription.

I would greatly appreciate an engineering investigation and a reliable resolution rather than generic advice to repeatedly switch models or reinstall the extension.

Thank you.

ChatGPT Plus.

### Which model were you using?

GPT-6.1-Sol, reasoning medium, provider openai.

### What platform is your computer?

Linux; local background server; collaboration mode Default. Permissions were Full Access at the time of the reported status. No subagents were launched during the work described below.

### What issue are you seeing?

The user reports that less than one hour of coding work used approximately half their available allowance, substantially faster than their experience with Sonnet 5.5 at medium reasoning.

Sanitized `/status` snapshot:

```text
Context window: 51% left (238K used / 475K)
5h limit: 56% left
Weekly limit: 57% left
```

Important measurement limitations: this is one end-of-session snapshot, not a before/after measurement. The starting allowance was not recorded, so the displayed percentages cannot establish the exact delta attributable to this session. The context-window figure is not a measurement of total billable tokens. No raw input/output/reasoning/cache token breakdown was collected. The Sonnet comparison is the user's qualitative experience, not a controlled benchmark.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Use GPT-6.1-Sol at medium in Codex CLI with a long-running TypeScript application conversation, project instructions and several screenshot-based UI requests.
2. Perform routine UI edits, a model-provider configuration change, financial goal comparison changes, and the required verification after code changes.
3. Run unit tests that take approximately 45–57 seconds and a full integration suite that takes approximately 462 seconds. Test output was redirected to local files.
4. Observe repeated short `write_stdin` polls requesting `yield_time_ms: 1000` (often returning after roughly 5 seconds), followed by separate `tail`/count commands on the same log files. Many calls add little new information while the same process is still running.
5. Inspect `/status` after the coding session.

The agent also repeatedly ran the full unit suite after small edits; project instructions explicitly required that verification, so that part is a workload factor rather than evidence of a bug by itself. The session had substantial instruction/context content, including duplicated project-instruction blocks. Its contribution to usage was not measured.

### What is the expected behavior?

Avoid excessive model turns and context growth while waiting for long-running tools. Prefer longer interruptible waits or completion notifications over repeated short polls and log rereads. Investigate whether prompt caching, context replay, reasoning usage or quota accounting explain the perceived disproportionate depletion, and expose enough usage detail to distinguish those causes.

### Codex doctor report

Not collected or attached: this report deliberately contains only manually selected, sanitized evidence.

### Additional information

No account email, personal name, project/repository identity, filesystem paths, session/thread identifiers, source code, screenshots or raw conversation logs are included. This issue body was prepared from the user's report and observable tool behavior with their authorization. Please treat the cause as unconfirmed.

Related reports found before filing: #55210 (Windows/Fast) and #51604 (macOS/Desktop). This report concerns Linux CLI/local background server at medium reasoning and includes repeated tool-polling behavior.

labels.name: bug

items.body:
### What version of the Codex App are you using (From “About Codex” dialog)?

26.1016.51333

### What subscription do you have?

Pro

### What platform is your computer?

_No response_

### What issue are you seeing?

Cloud workspace downloads stall after proxy CONNECT 200, before TLS completes. On 21 October, 11:37–11:39 UTC, both an allowed oaiusercontent.com staging host and a Dropbox download host timed out. A same-proxy chatgpt.com control succeeded with verified TLS. Restarting the workspace did not resolve it. Please investigate the managed proxy’s host policy and upstream DNS/routing/TLS handling.

HTTPS downloads into the assistant’s cloud workspace repeatedly time out before TLS completes. This affects both Dropbox temporary download links and files retrieved by the Google Drive connector and staged for transfer into the workspace.
The failure is in the cloud workspace, not my local PC. I use the ChatGPT web interface on Windows.
Impact
- New source documents cannot be downloaded for review.
- Previously uploaded review results cannot be downloaded for integrity verification.
- Upload operations have succeeded, but download verification remains blocked.
- Direct chat attachments can still be materialized into the workspace through the Library route.
Expected behaviour
An authorized download should complete with normal TLS certificate verification, producing the original file bytes so size and SHA-256 can be checked.
Actual behaviour
The configured proxy acknowledges CONNECT with HTTP 200, but TLS does not complete. No HTTPS response or file bytes arrive before the timeout.
Verified diagnostic results
Tests were performed on 21 October 2026, approximately 11:37–11:39 UTC, using bounded HEAD requests to hostname roots. No signed download paths or file contents were requested in these diagnostic tests.
1. Control: chatgpt.com
   - Proxy CONNECT: 200
   - TLS verification: successful
   - HTTPS response: 200
   - Total time: 0.222524 seconds
2. Drive connector staging host: sdmntprcentralus.oaiusercontent.com
   - Proxy CONNECT: 200
   - TLS completion: not reached
   - HTTPS response: none (curl HTTP code 000)
   - curl exit code: 28
   - Total time: 12.002572 seconds
   - time_appconnect, time_pretransfer and time_starttransfer: all zero
3. Dropbox temporary-download origin: a *.dl.dropboxusercontent.com host
   - Proxy CONNECT: 200
   - TLS completion: not reached
   - HTTPS response: none (curl HTTP code 000)
   - curl exit code: 28
   - Total time: 12.001034 seconds
   - Downloaded bytes: zero
   - Error: Connection timed out after 12000 milliseconds
Actual file-transfer observations
- Repeated bounded Dropbox GETs timed out after 40 seconds with zero bytes, including a small approximately 28 KB test manifest.
- The Google Drive connector found and retrieved a 62,264,598-byte PDF into its staging service. Transferring that staged file into the workspace then timed out after 120 seconds with zero bytes.
- The small manifest and hostname-only tests show that this is not simply a large-PDF transfer problem.
Troubleshooting already completed
- Restarted the workspace earlier that day; failures persisted afterward.
- Confirmed approximately 12 GiB of free workspace storage.
- Used the existing managed proxy and normal TLS verification throughout.
- Did not disable certificate verification, change CA trust, bypass the proxy, alter network permissions or change cloud-file access settings.
- Confirmed that Library server-side materialization works. This is a different transfer route and does not demonstrate that workspace HTTPS downloads work.
Important distinction
The Drive staging hostname matches the supplied workspace network allowlist. The Dropbox download hostname does not appear to match that visible list. A host-policy restriction could therefore contribute to Dropbox’s failure, but does not explain both failures from the visible configuration alone.
Both fail at the same observed stage, but a single shared root cause has not been proven. CONNECT 200 does not prove that the proxy established a working upstream TLS connection.
Investigation requested
Please inspect the managed proxy’s effective host-policy handling and upstream DNS, routing and TLS connection handling for these download destinations. Please also check whether a workspace provisioning or proxy-service issue can cause CONNECT to be acknowledged while the subsequent TLS handshake stalls.
Success criteria
A real authorized download completes with normal TLS verification, and the downloaded bytes match the saved expected size and SHA-256. Metadata access or CONNECT 200 alone is not sufficient.
Privacy
This report intentionally excludes signed URLs, tokens, private file names, file contents and client information.

items.body:
## Summary

On **October 21, 2026 (UTC+08:00)**, Codex repeatedly failed with **"Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model."** This affects **both ordinary task execution and remote context compaction**, rather than compaction alone.

These failures interrupt my ongoing coding/research workflow and can prevent Codex from completing even a normal request.

## Environment

- **Client:** Codex desktop app on Windows (exact app build not yet collected)
- **OS:** Windows; I also use WSL2 for development, but the errors appear in the Codex app UI and do **not** require running a GPU task
- **Model:** My prior Codex configuration used `gpt-6-astra`; the exact active model is not visible in the affected screenshots, so I cannot confirm that this is model-specific or affects all selectable models
- **First captured examples:** October 21, 2026, approximately **15:09–15:10 UTC+08:00**
- **Logs / feedback ID:** Not yet available

## Actual behavior

### Failure A — remote compaction

While using an existing Codex conversation, the UI displays:

```text
Error running remote compact task: Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.
```

The UI also shows **"优化已中断"** (optimization interrupted) and offers a retry option. The compaction task does not complete.

### Failure B — ordinary Codex task, without needing compaction

In a separate ordinary request, I asked Codex to check whether GitHub was connected and which connection methods were available. Codex began responding:

> 可以。我先检查当前是否已连接 GitHub，以及可用的连接方式……

After approximately **19 seconds**, the UI repeatedly displayed:

```text
Selected model is at capacity. Please try a different model.
```

The errors appeared on the task itself, with a **Retry** control. This is **not limited to long-context compaction**.

## Steps to reproduce (observed)

1. Open Codex Desktop on Windows while signed in.
2. In an existing conversation that invokes remote compaction, attempt to continue the task: compaction can fail with the full `Error running remote compact task` message.
3. Independently, submit an ordinary request (e.g., ask Codex to inspect the available GitHub connection methods).
4. Observe that a partial response can appear, followed by repeated `Selected model is at capacity` errors and a retry option.

**Reproduction frequency:** Repeatedly observed, but I have not measured an exact failure percentage.

## Expected behavior

Normal requests should execute successfully, and context compaction should complete when needed. If the service is genuinely at capacity, the app should recover gracefully and indicate a meaningful retry or fallback path rather than repeatedly blocking the workflow.

## Impact

- Interrupts long-running coding sessions and context management.
- Blocks normal research/programming tasks, including GitHub-related work.
- Makes sustained human–AI development workflows unreliable.

## Troubleshooting status and limitations

- I have seen repeated failures and retry controls.
- I have **not** yet verified whether changing models, re-authenticating, regenerating a passkey, or signing out of all sessions resolves the issue.
- I have **not** captured the exact Codex app version, request IDs, model backend, network route, or full local logs.
- I cannot determine from the UI alone whether the root cause is server capacity, request routing, authentication/session state, or another issue.

## Additional observations (possibly unrelated)

- Around the same period, my Dot has also intermittently become unresponsive. I do **not** know whether this shares a root cause with the Codex capacity errors.
- I have subjectively noticed reduced reasoning depth, consistency, or response quality compared with earlier use. This is **not independently benchmarked** and I am not claiming any proven change in model capabilities or reasoning allocation.

The reproducible Codex capacity errors above are the primary subject of this report.

## Related reports

- #55854 — capacity error reported for all available models in a Codex workspace
- #55857 — persistent errors across Codex Web, Desktop, and CLI
- #55740 — Windows user report of persistent capacity errors

I can provide the two UI screenshots and more diagnostic details if needed. Please let me know which **non-sensitive** logs or diagnostic identifiers would be most helpful.

items.title: [Dots][Cross-device Codex Desktop] Full Access selection confirms but does not apply to another computer's thread (ChatGPT Web works)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: sandbox
labels.description: Issues related to permissions or sandboxing

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

labels.name: dots
labels.description: Issues involving setting up ChatGPT dots or managing their ongoing work.

items.body:
## Summary

A Codex thread launched from **Dots** on **local computer A** starts with **Workspace Write** permissions. The same A-hosted thread is visible in the **Codex desktop app on local computer B**.

On B, changing that thread to **Full Access** appears to succeed: the desktop UI shows a confirmation. However, the change does **not** take effect for the thread running on A. By contrast, changing **the very same thread** to Full Access from **ChatGPT Web** also shows a confirmation **and does take effect**.

This is a cross-device, cross-client permission-update inconsistency, not simply a report about a default sandbox mode.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In **Dots**, start/open a Codex thread executing on connected **local computer A**. It initially has **Workspace Write** permissions.
2. On a **different computer B**, open the **Codex desktop app** under the same account and locate the thread hosted on A.
3. In B's Codex app, change the thread's permission/access mode from **Workspace Write** to **Full Access**.
4. Observe that the UI displays a **confirmation/success indication**.
5. Continue or check the same thread executing on A: the selected Full Access mode has **not actually taken effect**; execution remains restricted.
6. Open **the same A-hosted thread** in **ChatGPT Web** and change it to **Full Access**.
7. Observe the Web confirmation; this time Full Access **does take effect** for the thread running on A.

## Expected behavior

The permission setting selected in computer B's Codex app should be applied to the authoritative A-hosted thread and honored by subsequent execution, just as the equivalent change from ChatGPT Web is.

If cross-device permission escalation is intentionally unsupported or blocked by an enforced policy, the app should explain this and **must not present the operation as successfully applied**.

## Actual behavior

| Client used to modify the same thread | UI result | Effective result on computer A |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Codex desktop app on computer B | Confirmation/success indication | Full Access does **not** take effect |
| ChatGPT Web | Confirmation/success indication | Full Access **does** take effect |

## Environment

- Product/workflow: **Dots → connected local computer A → Codex thread**
- Controller 1: **Codex desktop app on another local computer B**
- Controller 2 (working comparison): **ChatGPT Web**
- Initial permission mode: **Workspace Write**
- Requested permission mode: **Full Access**
- Codex desktop versions and OS versions: **not yet captured**
- Effective sandbox settings/logs after each change: **not yet captured independently**; the observed difference is in whether the requested permission change actually takes effect

## Why this is worth investigating separately

The **same thread** can be upgraded successfully through ChatGPT Web but not from a different computer's Codex desktop app. This A/B comparison may help isolate a desktop remote-thread permission update/propagation or UI acknowledgement issue. No root cause is asserted.

## Related issues

- #50671 — Dot-created tasks show Full Access in desktop UI while delegated follow-up turns remain restricted. This report adds a **second local computer** as the desktop controller and a **working ChatGPT Web control on the identical thread**.
- #37570 — Cross-linked Desktop Remote/SSH views can unexpectedly change a remote thread's effective permissions. That report covers **downgrades from simply opening** a remote thread; this one covers **explicit Full Access selection that reports success but does not apply**.

No account identifiers, device names, private project paths, or thread contents are included. Additional version/build information or sanitized diagnostics can be supplied if requested.

items.title: Codex Windows: Projects disappear after update while records remain in local SQLite database

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: windows-os
labels.description: Issues related to Codex on Windows systems

items.body:
## Bug description

After a recent Codex Windows app update, all four of my previously configured local projects disappeared from the Projects sidebar. Their original records still exist in the local SQLite database, but the application does not display them.

The problem was first noticed on October 20, 2026. The projects had been accessible before the update.

Re-adding an existing project directory did not restore the original project. Instead, it created a new, empty project entry without the previous conversation history.

## Environment

- Operating system: Windows
- Codex app version reported in About: 26.1013.40934
- Release date shown in the app: October 16, 2026
- Windows AppX package version before update: 26.1013.3656.0
- Windows AppX package version after update: 26.1013.4894.0
- Successful update completion: October 19, 2026, at 17:55:41 local time (CEST, UTC+2)
- Problem first noticed: October 20, 2026

## Expected behavior

Previously configured local projects and their associated conversations should remain accessible after an application update.

Existing project directories should be recognized as their original projects rather than creating duplicate entries.

## Actual behavior

1. All four original projects disappeared from the Projects sidebar.
2. The Projects section remains enabled in the sidebar display settings.
3. Chats are sorted by Last updated.
4. Checking Archived chats did not reveal the missing project conversations.
5. Some recent conversations remain visible in the Windows application, while the web interface does not show the same conversation history.
6. Re-adding an existing project directory created a separate, empty project rather than restoring the original project and its conversations.

## Local diagnostic findings

Before investigating, I created a backup of the entire local `.codex` directory.

### SQLite database

The local `state_5.sqlite` database initially contained:

- 4 original project records.
- 4 corresponding project root records.
- Original project directories that still exist on disk.
- 15 thread records with NULL `project_id` values.

The recorded thread working directories did not match the four original project roots or their subdirectories. Therefore, I cannot confirm that these 15 thread records represent the missing project conversations.

After re-adding one original project directory, the number of project records increased from 4 to 5. The newly created project was empty, while the original project record remained in the database.

### Global state configuration

The `.codex-global-state.json` configuration contained the following values:

- `projectsMigrated: true`
- `threadAssignmentsMigrated: false`
- `pendingThreadAssignmentIds`: 2 entries
- `local-projects`: empty object
- `selected-project`: null

These values may be relevant to project and thread state migration, but I cannot confirm that they are the root cause.

## Windows update log findings

I examined the Windows AppXDeploymentServer operational event log.

The following events were recorded:

| Date and time (CEST) | Event |
| --- | --- |
| October 19, 2026, 00:09 | Update attempt failed with error 0x80073D02 because Codex was running |
| October 19, 2026, 15:04 | Another update attempt failed with the same error |
| October 19, 2026, 17:10 | Another update attempt failed with the same error |
| October 19, 2026, 17:55:41 | Deployment registration of package version 26.1013.4894.0 completed successfully |
| October 19–20, 2026 | Repeated error 0x12C events while attempting to delete files belonging to the previous package version |

The update occurred shortly before the disappearance was noticed. However, the event log alone does not establish that the update caused the issue.

## Steps to reproduce

I cannot reliably reproduce the original disappearance on demand.

The observed sequence was:

1. Use Codex for Windows with four configured local projects and their conversations.
2. Allow Windows to update the Codex application.
3. Open Codex and observe that the original projects are missing from the sidebar.
4. Re-add one of the original project directories using the application's project selection functionality.
5. Observe that a new, empty project is created instead of restoring the original project and its history.
6. Inspect the local SQLite database and confirm that both the original and newly created project records exist.

## Troubleshooting already performed

- Verified the correct account and workspace.
- Checked the sidebar display settings and confirmed that Projects is enabled.
- Checked chat sorting, which is set to Last updated.
- Checked Archived chats.
- Verified that the original project records remain in SQLite.
- Verified that the original project directories still exist.
- Tested re-adding one original project directory, resulting in a duplicate.
- Examined the global state configuration.
- Examined the Windows AppX deployment event log.
- Created a backup of the local `.codex` directory.
- Did not manually modify the SQLite database or JSON configuration.

No further project directories have been re-added to avoid creating additional duplicate records.

## Feedback / diagnostic reference

A feedback report has already been submitted through the Codex application with diagnostic logs enabled.

The feedback session ID is available upon request and can be shared privately with the OpenAI support or engineering team.

## Request

Could you investigate whether the Windows application update, local project state migration, or project-to-thread association handling could cause existing local projects to disappear from the user interface while their records remain in SQLite?

I would particularly appreciate guidance on a safe recovery procedure that preserves the original project records and conversation history without resetting, reinstalling, or manually modifying the application data.

I can provide additional sanitized diagnostic information if needed.

items.title: [Desktop][MCP Apps] Allow global entrypoints to request composer presentation, start minimized, or omit the host composer

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
### What variant of Codex are you using?

ChatGPT/Codex desktop app on Windows, with a third-party MCP plugin exposing a `global` entrypoint. The installed package inspected during this investigation was `OpenAI.Codex 26.1016.6573.0`.

### What feature would you like to see?

Please provide a documented, supported way for MCP apps/plugins to request the initial visibility and presentation of the host composer on their global entrypoints, including an optional mode that omits the host composer entirely for that surface.

The use case is Operator Studio, a repository-local artifact viewer and development workspace with its own structured prompt-authoring UI. The host's floating composer can overlap the plugin's content and controls, and manually minimizing it on each visit interrupts the workflow.

Related: #54241 reports a floating host composer covering the tldraw plugin's drawing toolbar. This request addresses the underlying integration capability: a supported, entrypoint-scoped contract for plugin authors.

### Requested behavior

1. **Start minimized on every open.** Allow a global entrypoint to request a minimized host composer each time the user opens it. The user should still be able to expand the composer during that visit. This initial-state policy should not require persisting composer-view changes, and a previously expanded state should not override the requested minimized start on the next open.

2. **Request composer presentation through a public interface.** Provide documented entrypoint metadata and/or a widget-to-host API for requesting the host composer's presentation. Please document supported values, capability detection, and how the host reports an unsupported or declined request. This should be available to third-party MCP plugins without access to a private first-party bridge.

3. **Optionally omit the host composer for the entrypoint.** Allow a plugin surface to request no host composer at all: no expanded editor, no minimized composer launcher, and no layout space reserved for it. Related composer overlays should not continue to obscure the plugin. This mode should apply only while that entrypoint is active; leaving it must restore the normal host behavior for the destination surface. It should not disable the plugin or remove its own UI.

### API proposal — illustrative only, not an existing supported API

The names `composerVisible` and `composerPresentation` below are **proposed public API fields**. They are not presented as currently supported MCP metadata or widget requests. In particular, `"disabled"` is a **proposed new value**, not a verified existing presentation option.

For a minimized initial state, the desired semantics could be expressed as:

```json
{
  "composerVisible": false
}
```

For a surface with no host composer, the proposed semantics could be expressed as:

```json
{
  "composerVisible": false,
  "composerPresentation": "disabled"
}
```

These fragments intentionally do not prescribe a metadata namespace or RPC method. A separate field for composer availability, or a different API shape, would also be fine. The important distinction is between **initially minimized but available** and **omitted for the active plugin surface**.

Please clarify whether any supported mechanism already provides these behaviors. If not, could OpenAI expose an entrypoint-scoped API for them, including lifecycle semantics for opening, leaving, and reopening the surface?

items.title: Existing remote MCP plugin retains old tool inventory after server update; new connection exposes added tool

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: mcp
labels.description: Issues related to the use of model context protocol (MCP) servers

labels.name: app
labels.description: Issues related to the Codex desktop app

items.body:
## Summary

An existing custom remote MCP plugin connection continued exposing its original 10 tools to a Codex cloud conversation after the server added an 11th tool. Creating and attaching a second connection to the same service made the new tool discoverable and callable in that same conversation.

This blocked cloud-side execution and required manual connection recreation. Please investigate tool-inventory invalidation/refresh for existing remote plugin connections.

## Environment

- Client: Codex desktop app on macOS, using a cloud conversation and custom remote MCP plugins.
- Exact Codex app build, macOS version, and subscription tier: not captured.
- Observed on October 21, 2026. All times below are Asia/Shanghai (UTC+08:00).
- Existing plugin name: `RN-WIN`; replacement connection: `RN-WIN-V2`.
- The affected tool is a custom application action, `windows_enter_desktop`, with an empty argument schema.
- The original read-only tool, `windows_system_status`, remained available and callable.

## Observed reproduction

1. Connect a custom remote MCP service that initially exposes 10 tools.
2. Update that service to add `windows_enter_desktop({})`, preserving the existing tool names and schemas.
3. Continue using the existing plugin connection in the cloud conversation.
4. Inspect the actual callable tool catalog, including deferred tools, across subsequent conversation turns.
5. Observe that the original connection still exposes only the old 10 tools; the new action is absent.
6. Create a second plugin connection to the updated service and attach it to the same conversation.
7. Observe that the second connection exposes the added action and that a real invocation reaches the application executor.

The new connection did not appear in the first checked turn after being mentioned. It appeared on a subsequent turn. This is an observation, not evidence of a guaranteed one-turn delay.

## Evidence and timeline

| Time | Observation |
| --- | --- |
| 18:12:45 | The deployment-side collaborator reported production deployment complete and server-side MCP validation of the added action. This is deployment-side evidence, separate from the cloud observations below. |
| 18:33:24–25 | The cloud conversation successfully called the original `windows_system_status({})`. Its response included newly deployed `daily_entry` fields, showing that updated response data was reachable through the existing connection. However, the cloud callable catalog still lacked `windows_enter_desktop`. |
| Subsequent turns | Repeated catalog inspections continued showing the original connection's 10 tools. The agent did not attempt to invoke an unregistered/guessed tool name. |
| 18:56 | The newly attached V2 connection exposed `mcp__codex_apps__rn_win_v2_windows_enter_desktop`, while the old namespace still lacked the equivalent tool. Both namespaces were visible in the same conversation. |
| 18:56:39–18:57:24 | A real cloud invocation of the V2 action reached the production executor and returned a structured application result. A subsequent read-only query confirmed the matching production record. |

The application result was `app_templates_not_unique`, with `clicked_enter=false` and `actions_this_call=0`. That is a separate application-level UI-matching failure. It confirms successful tool discovery and dispatch through V2; it is **not** evidence that the requested desktop action succeeded.

## Expected behavior

After a server's tool inventory changes, the existing connection should have a supported way to refresh/re-discover the current tools and expose them to the conversation without requiring a replacement plugin connection.

If catalog changes require explicit refresh, reattachment, or a new conversation, the UI/documentation should make that requirement clear and report whether refresh has completed or failed.

## Actual behavior and impact

The existing connection could read updated response fields but continued advertising the older tool inventory. The user had to create and attach another connection to unblock discovery of the new action. This caused repeated troubleshooting and delayed cloud-side acceptance.

## Limits of this report

- We did not capture server `notifications/tools/list_changed` traffic or prove that such a notification was emitted.
- We did not capture the platform's internal discovery/refresh requests, cache entries, or connection metadata.
- We do not have a verified UI Refresh request/response trace for this specific server update, so this report does not claim a particular Refresh-button implementation failed.
- Cache invalidation, per-connection metadata, and conversation-level inventory lifetime are possible investigation areas, not confirmed root causes.
- This is an observed workflow in an existing installation, not a clean-install minimal reproduction.
- No credentials, service addresses, private conversation IDs, screenshots, or raw application logs are included.

## Related report

Possibly related: #35583 (Desktop MCP tool refresh after `notifications/tools/list_changed`). That report concerns stdio and verified notifications; this report concerns a custom remote plugin connection and the old-connection/new-connection contrast. The same root cause has not been established.

items.body:
## Summary

Excel Live Control session discovery is blocked in the ChatGPT/Codex Windows workflow because the document-control MCP tool is visible to the assistant in the integration catalog but is **not available to the model** when invoked.

Exact error:

```text
MCP tool `codex_apps/codex_document_control.list_document_sessions` is not available to the model
```

This occurs **before** Codex can enumerate document sessions or read any workbook cells. It is distinct from the `403: arc control transport is not enabled` symptom described in #55474.

## Environment

- ChatGPT desktop app on Windows; version **26.1016.51333** (user reports installing the update dated **20 October 2026**).
- Microsoft Excel **Microsoft 365** desktop.
- Official **ChatGPT** Office add-in by OpenAI installed, open in Excel, and signed in.
- ChatGPT Settings > Computer Use: **Microsoft Excel** access enabled; **Any App** access enabled; Excel shown under always-allowed applications.
- **Spreadsheets** plugin verified as installed and enabled.
- Reproduced on **21 October 2026**.
- Windows build, Codex runtime build, and rollout/transport state were not independently verified.

## Reproduction / observations

1. Open an Excel workbook and the signed-in official ChatGPT add-in pane.
2. Verify the add-in itself works: user tested reading cells **A1:C1**, including a formula, successfully from **inside Excel**. Test values were A1 = `TEST-123`, B1 = `17`, C1 = `=B1*2` (evaluating to 34).
3. In a Codex conversation in the Windows ChatGPT app, ask to read cells A1:C1 **only through Excel Live Control**, explicitly without Computer Use, mouse, or keyboard actions.
4. Codex reports that `codex_apps/codex_document_control.list_document_sessions` is listed in the integration catalog, but invocation fails with the exact `not available to the model` error above.
5. Codex cannot discover the connected workbook/session and does not read cells or modify the workbook. The direct-control attempt did **not** use Computer Use.

## Expected

With the official add-in signed in, enabled Excel access, and the Spreadsheets plugin present, Codex should be able to invoke document-session discovery (or clearly identify any required availability/entitlement prerequisite) and then read the connected workbook through the dedicated document-control channel.

## Actual

The assistant cannot invoke the session-discovery tool at all. This error does **not** establish whether Excel itself is connected, whether a transport is enabled, or why the tool was not exposed to this model/session.

## Related reports

- #55474 — document control session discovery returns **403: arc control transport is not enabled** (different error, possibly related layer).
- #36836 — Excel live-control skill should attempt lazy tool discovery before suggesting reinstall/new chat.
- #54104 — other Codex Windows connected tools have reported **`not available to the model`**.

Could maintainers clarify why this tool is advertised but not invokable, and what supported diagnostic or recovery procedure applies? No workbook/client identifiers, paths, account details, tokens, logs, or screenshots are attached.

_Reported with the affected user's authorization._
